title: Orders to Write the Sikh Origin for London

blocks.text: The second episode places the Sikh story before imperial scrutiny by describing an English general's demand for a reliable account. He orders Bootey Shah Maulvi to write the Sikh origin truthfully for London so that the rise of Sikh power can be understood rather than guessed at from rumor.

The narrator is uneasy about this assignment, because a Muslim court writer may not gladly celebrate the Panth's glory or sovereignty. That tension gives the page its shape: the history is being commissioned from outside while also being defended from distortion from within.

The result is a self-aware account of historical transmission. Sikh origins are not merely remembered locally; they are being prepared as evidence for readers in colonial and royal circles who demand explanation.
